title: Gear Train
summary: Crank a clockwork machine at the right speed so its last gear hits a target rate: chain rule, exponentials, implicit and second derivatives.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 5.3, Differentiability (chain rule, implicit, parametric, second order)
concepts: Derivatives of e^x, a^x and ln x
learningOutcome: The student can find the derivative of a composite, exponential, implicit or parametric function at a point and the second derivative, and use it as a rate: output rate = derivative × input rate.

levels.title: Layers of gears
levels.adds: Baseline: the chain rule on powers of linear and quadratic expressions at a point; output rate = derivative × crank rate (Ex 5.2 Q1 to Q8).
hints: Peel the layers from the outside in and multiply the derivatives.
First find the derivative at the given x, then divide the target rate by it.
d/dx of (ax + b)ⁿ is n·a·(ax + b)ⁿ⁻¹.

levels.title: Exponent and log gears
levels.adds: New: derivatives of e^g, ln g and a^g, with the output counted in units of e to a power or of ln a (Ex 5.4 Q2 to Q8; Ex 5.5).
hints: d/dx e^g = g′·e^g: the target is a multiple of e^g(x₀).
d/dx ln g = g′/g, which is a fraction at a point.
d/dx a^g = a^g·(ln a)·g′, so the target is a multiple of ln a.

levels.title: Beads and drones
levels.adds: New: implicit curves and parametric curves, where the slope comes from differentiating both sides or from (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) (Ex 5.3 Q1 to Q8; Ex 5.6).
hints: On x² + y² = r², differentiate both sides: 2x + 2y·y′ = 0.
For parametric curves divide dy/dt by dx/dt, then evaluate at the given t.
The y rate is the slope times the x rate w.

levels.title: Acceleration
levels.adds: New: the second derivative as an acceleration, which depends on w² (Ex 5.7 Q1 to Q8).
hints: x moves steadily, so x″ = 0 and y″ = f″(x)·w².
Differentiate twice, then put in x.
Divide the target by f″ and take the square root.

misconceptions: The derivative of a composite is the product of the outer and inner functions
The derivative of e^(x²) is e^(x²)
Doubling the speed doubles the acceleration
